risks: model ranking does not hold across windows
only 3 validation windows: weight estimation is high variance
diagnosis.narrative: The series is dominated by a strong upward trend (a net rise of ~220% of its level). A moderate seasonal pattern is present. The series is quite predictable: its energy concentrates in a few structured frequencies. The series reads as non-stationary by the ADF/KPSS tests. Across validation windows the model ranking is unstable (Kendall tau 0.29), which favours a robust combination.

Test a weighted average using inverse error on the most stable pool (pool3) to see if it improves over the best single model.
Test a robust median over the most stable models (pool1) to see if it improves over the best single.
Test a robust aggregate on a stable subset – median over pool2.
Test a robust median combination over the most stable pool (pool3) to see if it beats the best single model.
Test a trimmed_mean over pool4 to see if trimming improves over weighted.
Test a simple mean over the most stable pool (pool4) to see if it beats the trimmed‑mean and weighted variants.
Test a robust median over the stable pool4 to see if it beats the current mean.
Test a DTW barycenter (dba) over pool4 to see if it beats weighted and mean; it's a new strategy.
Test a DTW barycenter over the smaller pool1 to see if fewer models improve alignment and reduce error.
Test a DTW barycenter over pool2 to see if a slightly larger pool improves over pool1 and pool4.
Test a DTW barycenter over pool3 to see if it improves over the best single and other weighted methods.

decision.justification: Selected 'best_single ONLY_CWT_catboost' (an agent proposal) as the best of 22 backtested attempts, score 0.225. Series context: trend strength 0.9912 and seasonal strength 0.3124; model ranking is unstable across windows (Kendall tau 0.29); 9 of 19 models carry independent error; relative error spread across the pool is 51.811.
